widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

accelerators:catalog.title: Programs
accelerators:catalog.description: Every tracked programme as a card: who runs it and where, the operator's own description, then the deal in mono with duration, funding offered, equity stance and batch size, and finally focus tags and a link. Every facet on the page narrows this list, under free-text search over names, operators and descriptions. Terms show exactly what the operator publishes, so a blank term is unstated rather than zero. The link goes to an application page where one exists, otherwise the programme's own page. Foreign-run programmes are included because Israeli founders enter them.

accelerators:map.title: Where They Run
accelerators:map.description: Programmes by their operator's registered city, taken from the company registry. Dot size is the number of programmes matching the current filters, clicking a city narrows to it, and hovering names that city's operators. Israel and Abroad above the map filter by the side of the world a programme runs from and always add up to the filtered catalogue. Operators whose registry address did not resolve to a city are counted off-map under Israel rather than placed on a guess.

accelerators:operators.title: Operators
accelerators:operators.description: The organisations running the programmes, ranked by how many match the current filters, with a meter showing the shape of it: most run a single programme and a handful run five or more. Clicking an operator filters the catalogue to its programmes. Location is the operator's registered city wherever the registry resolves one.

accelerators:cost.title: What It Costs
accelerators:cost.description: Programme type against stated equity stance: takes no equity, takes equity, or silent. Each cell is that type's share sitting in that stance, with the type's programme count beside its name because the percentages are shares of that number. Clicking a cell narrows to that pair, a type name to the whole type, a column header to that stance across every type. Operators that take equity publish terms less often, so treat the equity-free share as a floor. Pilots are left out because a pilot places a product with a corporate, with no cheque and no cap table, and stay reachable from the operators card.

accelerators:funding.title: Funding Offered
accelerators:funding.description: Programmes banded by the funding their operator states it offers, four ordered bands scaled against the largest. Clicking a band filters the list. Amounts are the operator's published offer, usually the top of a range. The count of programmes publishing no amount sits on the title line and filters too, kept off the chart because it is the large majority and would flatten the distribution this card exists to show.

accelerators:focus.title: Focus Areas
accelerators:focus.description: The operators' own declared sectors, folded onto a dozen buckets and sized by how many programs match the current filters. Clicking narrows the list; several can be active at once. 'Undeclared' is real: an operator that publishes no sector focus, which is not the same as generalist.

accelerators:calendar.title: Published Dates
accelerators:calendar.description: What operators publish about timing: a twelve-month grid of start dates and application deadlines where clicking a month filters the list, then the next three dated programmes with the soonest actionable event first. Clicking one pins the catalogue to it. Few operators publish forward dates, so an empty month means nothing published rather than nothing running, and undated programmes stay reachable through every other facet.
